section_summary: This section concerns postwar Japanese fisheries, especially proposals to expand fishing grounds and arrangements for the 1947–48 Antarctic whaling expedition. It includes diplomatic exchanges about whaling rules, observers, vessels, fuel and radar, alongside reports on Japan’s fishing industry and correspondence with American fishing interests.

subfiles.title: Department telegram on off-Kamchatka fishing talks
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The Department conditionally permits exploratory talks on extending Japanese fishing off Kamchatka.
subfiles.summary: Warns that fisheries proposals could complicate peace treaty and Far Eastern Commission discussions; requests objectives and an assessment before negotiations conclude.

subfiles.title: SCAP request for views on northern fishing extension
subfiles.about: SCAP asks whether a proposal to extend Japanese fishing northward should be prepared for other powers.
subfiles.summary: Requests the Department’s current view on fishing off Kamchatka.

subfiles.title: Whaling vessels for the 1947–48 Antarctic season
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits SCAP’s vessel list and notes that Settsu Maru will accompany the expedition.
subfiles.summary: Forwards vessel details supplied to the British liaison mission.

subfiles.title: Details of vessels for the Japanese Antarctic whaling expedition
subfiles.to: Head of United Kingdom Liaison Mission in Japan
subfiles.about: Lists planned factory ships, catchers, transports and tankers with their gross tonnages.
subfiles.summary: A further salted-meat transport had yet to be chosen.

subfiles.title: Conversation on Australian whaling proposal
subfiles.about: Bullock questions the consistency of United States statements rejecting Australia’s proposed operation of a Japanese whaling unit.
subfiles.summary: Fearey explains the timing of Department review and Far Eastern Commission discussion. Bullock says Australia expects no further diplomatic protest but may act in the Commission.

subfiles.title: Armour letter to Senator Knowland on Japanese peace treaty fisheries
subfiles.about: Addresses Knowland’s interest in proposed fisheries provisions for the Japanese peace treaty.
subfiles.summary: Assures him that West Coast fishing concerns are receiving consideration.

subfiles.title: Japanese Antarctic whaling correspondence
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits British questions about Japanese Antarctic whaling and SCAP’s response.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the September 1 British communication and September 16 reply.

subfiles.title: British questions on Antarctic whaling controls
subfiles.from: A. Gascoigne, United Kingdom Liaison Mission
subfiles.about: Seeks assurances on treaty rules, catch reports, flags and recovery of whale marks.
subfiles.summary: Asks SCAP to instruct Japanese authorities on the protocol and communicate catch statistics promptly.

subfiles.title: SCAP reply on Antarctic whaling controls
subfiles.about: Answers British questions about the protocol, catch reporting, flags, whale marks and Settsu Maru.
subfiles.summary: States that SCAP will oversee reports and the Japanese will search for marked whales.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Senator Knowland’s fisheries concerns
subfiles.about: Records Knowland’s request for fishing industry consultation on Japanese peace treaty proposals.
subfiles.summary: Flory describes existing contacts and recommends consulting interested senators and Congressman Tollefson before treaty negotiations.

subfiles.title: Letter to Senator Knowland enclosing treaty proposals
subfiles.about: Sends Knowland a memorandum on possible fisheries provisions for the Japanese peace treaty.
subfiles.summary: Says the Department has reached no final conclusion.

subfiles.title: SCAP reply on off-Kamchatka negotiations
subfiles.about: SCAP considers local talks on off-Kamchatka fishing unproductive and inadvisable.
subfiles.summary: Says Fisheries Division chief Herrington will discuss the matter in Washington.

subfiles.title: Petroleum products for Antarctic whaling vessels
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits SCAP instructions governing petroleum supplies for the whaling expedition.
subfiles.summary: Encloses SCAPIN 1781.

subfiles.title: SCAP petroleum authorization for the whaling expedition
subfiles.about: Authorizes specified fuel and lubricants for the 1947–48 Antarctic whaling expedition.
subfiles.summary: Rescinds earlier petroleum memoranda, sets quantities and receipt procedures, and requires a plan for fleet movements, cargoes and unloading fuel.

subfiles.title: Routing note on reply to Army fisheries letter
subfiles.about: Suggests acknowledging the Army’s fisheries proposal while it receives further consideration.
subfiles.summary: Handwritten advice on the form of a reply.

subfiles.title: Army letter forwarding SCAP study of fishing areas
subfiles.about: Forwards Herrington’s memorandum on expanding permitted Japanese fishing areas.
subfiles.summary: Asks State to help secure favorable action on practical expansion proposals.

subfiles.title: Japanese fishing areas
subfiles.to: Special Assistant to the Secretary of the Army
subfiles.about: Reviews northern, Yellow Sea and offshore Pacific possibilities for expanding Japanese fishing.
subfiles.summary: Describes gear shortages and the projected production ceiling in current waters. Notes Soviet and Korean obstacles and a proposal for tuna grounds toward Midway and the equator.

subfiles.title: Draft reply to Colonel Laux
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the Army’s memorandum on wider Japanese fishing areas.
subfiles.summary: Says State will remain in contact with the Army as developments warrant.

subfiles.title: Reply to Colonel Laux on fishing area expansion
subfiles.about: Responds to the Army’s request concerning expansion of Japanese fishing grounds.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges the economic importance of wider fishing and promises further communication.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of report on the Japanese fishing industry
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a SCAP Civil Information and Education report on Japanese fisheries.
subfiles.summary: Encloses five copies of The Fishing Industry.

subfiles.title: The Fishing Industry
subfiles.from: SCAP Civil Information and Education Section
subfiles.about: Surveys Japanese magazine discussion of fish supply, distribution, materials, fishing cooperatives and companies.
subfiles.summary: Reports optimism about expanded catches alongside shortages of oil, nets and hemp. Summarizes arguments over price controls, coastal cooperatives and commercial firms.

subfiles.title: Additional whaling protocol for Japan
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits a SCAP directive applying another international whaling protocol to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Encloses SCAPIN 1785.

subfiles.title: Whaling Industry
subfiles.about: Adds the December 1946 Washington protocol and conference Final Act to Japanese whaling instructions.
subfiles.summary: Amends SCAP’s earlier whaling directive.

subfiles.title: Spectator article on whaling
subfiles.from: Everett F. Drumright, American Embassy London
subfiles.about: Forwards a Spectator article opposing relaxation of Antarctic whaling limits and criticizing Japanese methods.
subfiles.summary: Highlights the article’s conservation argument and charges of waste.

subfiles.title: Whale-Hunting Folly
subfiles.about: Argues for strict Antarctic catch limits and faults Japanese whaling practices.
subfiles.summary: Cites declining whale fertility and size, then alleges waste and poor oil yields in the Japanese expedition. Calls for enforceable international restrictions.

subfiles.title: Reply on Allied whaling observers’ expenses
subfiles.about: Rejects Britain’s request to pay Allied observers from the Japanese whaling expedition’s proceeds.
subfiles.summary: Reaffirms SCAP’s view that sending governments should initially bear salaries and expenses, potentially as occupation costs. Argues the arrangement does not subsidize Japanese whaling companies.

subfiles.title: British request on whaling inspectors’ expenses
subfiles.about: Asks that inspectors’ costs be paid from proceeds of the forthcoming Japanese Antarctic expedition.
subfiles.summary: Compares British license-funded inspectors and questions whether sending states would subsidize Japanese companies.

subfiles.title: Illegible file leaf
subfiles.about: The page contains only fragmentary numbers and no recoverable document text.
subfiles.summary: No substantive text is legible.

subfiles.title: SCAP message maintaining earlier position
subfiles.about: States that the reasons in an earlier message still apply.
subfiles.summary: A brief response referring to message W 89288.

subfiles.title: SCAP telegram on British whaling inspectors
subfiles.about: Explains rations, arrival dates and payment arrangements for British inspectors on the 1946–47 expedition.
subfiles.summary: Says inspectors’ salaries are occupation costs and authorizes two British inspectors.

subfiles.title: Del Mar inquiry about albacore operations near Saipan
subfiles.about: Requests advice on developing albacore supply and shore facilities near Saipan.
subfiles.summary: Describes unsuccessful purchasing efforts in Japan and interest in fishing grounds near the former mandated islands.

subfiles.title: Reply to Del Mar on Saipan fisheries
subfiles.about: Responds to Del Mar’s inquiry about fisheries facilities near Saipan.
subfiles.summary: Says policy remains under consideration and offers a discussion in Washington.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Herrington on fishing area expansion
subfiles.about: Records Herrington’s possible revisions to Far Eastern Commission fishing-area policy.
subfiles.summary: Discusses coastal consent requirements and a possible uniform Pacific exclusion line.

subfiles.title: Registration and marking of Japanese fishing vessels
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits SCAP’s directive for registering and marking Japanese fishing vessels.
subfiles.summary: Encloses SCAPIN 1809.

subfiles.title: Instructions for registration and marking of Japanese fishing vessels
subfiles.about: Establishes registration, marking and statistical reporting rules for Japanese fishing vessels.
subfiles.summary: Defines covered vessels and waters, prescribes applications, registration cards, identification numbers and vessel classes. Requires prefectural and national statistics and provides penalties for false records or other violations.

subfiles.title: Army request for action on wider Japanese fishing grounds
subfiles.about: Urges action on northern, Yellow Sea and offshore Pacific fishing proposals.
subfiles.summary: Reports Herrington’s estimates and political obstacles. Favors pursuing Yellow Sea access and tuna grounds toward Midway and the equator.

subfiles.title: Draft reply to Johnson on fishing area proposals
subfiles.about: Responds to the Army’s three proposals for extending Japanese fishing.
subfiles.summary: Finds northern access unlikely, discusses Korean interests in the Yellow Sea, and identifies possibilities and obstacles for offshore Pacific expansion.

subfiles.title: Alternative draft reply to Johnson
subfiles.about: Drafts a response on the same three possible extensions of Japanese fishing.
subfiles.summary: Reviews northern, Korean-adjacent and offshore high-seas areas.

subfiles.title: Oslo request for Japanese whaling data
subfiles.about: Renews a request for data on Japanese whaling at Bonin Islands during 1946–47.
subfiles.summary: Says the International Whaling Statistics office is still awaiting the information.

subfiles.title: London airgram on parliamentary whaling assurance
subfiles.about: Asks State to verify Bevin’s statement on consultations before another Japanese Antarctic whaling expedition.
subfiles.summary: Quotes a House of Commons exchange and requests confirmation.

subfiles.title: Department reply to London on Japanese whaling
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission London
subfiles.about: Sends earlier British and American aide-mémoires about Japanese Antarctic whaling.
subfiles.summary: Transmits copies for the Embassy’s information.

subfiles.title: Record-copy replacement form for Tokyo despatch 1389
subfiles.about: Designates a replacement record copy for an unreturned action copy.
subfiles.summary: Identifies Tokyo despatch 1389.

subfiles.title: Radio communications for Japanese whaling fleet
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits a SCAP directive on radio communications for Japanese whaling vessels.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the November 4 directive, whose text is not present here.

subfiles.title: SCAP request for whaling inspectors’ logbook
subfiles.about: Records efforts to identify forms requested by SCAP for whaling inspectors.
subfiles.summary: Concludes that SCAP’s own daily catch forms may meet the request.

subfiles.title: Conversation presenting Norwegian whaling aide-mémoire
subfiles.about: Records Lykke’s presentation of Norwegian concerns about Japanese oil yields and alleged violations.
subfiles.summary: Also notes discussion of surplus fish negotiations and the status of the 1946 protocol.

subfiles.title: Norwegian analysis of Japanese whaling
subfiles.about: Compares Japanese and Norwegian whale-oil yields and cites alleged violations aboard Hashidate Maru.
subfiles.summary: Presents a statistical adjustment for retained blubber and quotes the Australian observer’s account of discarded bones and oil-rich ribs.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Norwegian whaling concerns to Tokyo
subfiles.to: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Requests that SCAP receive the Norwegian Embassy’s whaling aide-mémoire.
subfiles.summary: Encloses two copies of the November 20 aide-mémoire.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Norwegian whaling aide-mémoire
subfiles.about: Advises Norway that its analysis and allegations are being sent to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges the November 20 communication.

subfiles.title: Del Mar follow-up on Guam representative
subfiles.about: Says A. B. Won Pat may visit State to discuss Del Mar’s Pacific fisheries project.
subfiles.summary: Requests that any new information be passed to Won Pat.

subfiles.title: Reply to Del Mar concerning Trust Territory fisheries
subfiles.about: Reports no new fisheries policy and offers to meet Won Pat about future commercial activity.
subfiles.summary: Invites discussion during Won Pat’s Washington visit.

subfiles.title: Record-copy replacement form for Tokyo despatch 1413
subfiles.about: Designates a replacement record copy for an unreturned action copy.
subfiles.summary: Identifies Tokyo despatch 1413.

subfiles.title: Soviet objection to radar aboard Japanese whalers
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits a Soviet inquiry, American reply and SCAP directive concerning radar on Japanese whalers.
subfiles.summary: Describes the dispute over whether navigational radar violates Far Eastern Commission restrictions.

subfiles.title: Soviet inquiry about Japanese whaling radar
subfiles.about: Questions SCAP’s reported permission to fit Japanese whaling vessels with former naval radar.
subfiles.summary: Cites Far Eastern Commission restrictions on Japanese possession of combat equipment.

subfiles.title: Sebald reply on Japanese whaling radar
subfiles.about: Explains SCAP’s supervised use of navigational radar aboard Japanese whalers.
subfiles.summary: Says Japanese ownership is not contemplated and the authorization does not extend to other vessels or radar development.
